statement: A cube has a different number from 1 to 6 on each face. In one position it shows 1 on top, 3 at the front and 4 on the right. In another position it shows 2 on top, 5 at the front and 4 on the right. Which number is on the face opposite 3?

choices.misconception: I worked out the ring of faces around 4 but put 2 and 5 in the wrong order around it.
I assumed opposite faces add up to 7, as on a standard die, although 4 is shown right next to 3.
I thought 6, the only number never shown, must be on the face opposite 3.
I thought two views of a cube could never fix where all six numbers are.

hints: Both views show 4 on the right. Look from the side of 4.
With 4 facing you, the other four faces form a ring around it. Each view shows two neighbouring faces of that ring, top then front, in order. Fit both pairs into one ring.
Turning the cube about the axis through 4 moves the ring round. The ring contains 1 followed by 3, and 2 followed by 5, in the same direction, so it must be 1, 3, 2, 5.

solutions.reliable: In both views 4 is on the right, so the second position is the first turned about the axis through face 4. Around face 4 lie four faces in a ring: top, front, bottom, back. The first view says that, going top then front, the ring contains 1 then 3. The second view says it contains 2 then 5, in the same direction. The only ring with both is 1, 3, 2, 5 (going top, front, bottom, back in the first view). So the bottom in the first view is 2 and the back is 5. Opposite faces are 1 and 2, 3 and 5, and 4 and 6 (the left face). The face opposite 3 is 5. The transferable idea: when two views share a face, read the ring of faces around it and fit the views into one ring.

whyOnTest: Cube views test spatial reasoning: a shared face fixes an axis, and the faces round it must fit one consistent ring.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
